messages:
sam: Customer on hosted API sees intermittent 502 when streaming /v1/streams/generate. Happens ~1/50 requests. Request id 0fb3c2a7 seen in our edge logs. Need a reproducible curl to escalate.

jenny: can you paste the raw request id and the client timestamp window? Also are they behind a corporate proxy or doing NATed egress? :thinking:

sam: Request id 0fb3c2a7, client time 2024-10-02T16:12:44Z. They confirmed corp proxy in front.

dev-support-bot: Note: Incident auto-tagged P2. If customer can attach trace bundle we'll prioritize.

jenny: OK — let's ask them to run a minimal streaming curl (mask tokens) and capture a trace. Share this snippet and ask for the trace + headers file.

jenny: ```
# minimal streaming reproduction we request them to run (replace token with REDACTED)
curl -N -v \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Client-Time: 2024-10-02T16:12:44Z" \
  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/streams/generate?model=llama-oas" \
  --data-raw '{"input":"hello","stream":true}' \
  --trace-ascii curl-trace.txt --dump-header headers.txt
```

jenny: Ask them to attach curl-trace.txt and headers.txt and to NOT paste raw tokens (they can redact). Also ask them to include the exact command they ran.

igor: Add these validation prompts: 1) run `curl -I` against the non-streaming /v1/outputs endpoint to confirm server headers (we want to see X-Request-Id or lack thereof), 2) run the streaming curl with `--proxy` if they use one so we reproduce path, 3) try `--http2` and `-v` to capture ALPN/TLS details.

sam: Customer replied: they ran similar curl, got immediate 502 and headers.txt is empty (no X-Request-Id). trace shows `recv() returned 0` after TLS handshake and then TCP FIN.

jenny: That points to an upstream outage or proxy terminating early. Request they run again with `-H "X-Debug-Collect: 1"` — that toggles extra correlation data in our edge and will include debug-id in logs so we can find internal traces even if no X-Request-Id returned.

jenny: Also ask them to run a non-stream simple POST (same payload, stream:false) to see if streaming path is specific:

jenny: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/outputs?model=llama-oas" \
  --data-raw '{"input":"hello","stream":false}' --trace-ascii curl-nostream-trace.txt --dump-header headers-nostream.txt
```

igor: If they can capture network-level info, request a short tcpdump around the call window: `sudo tcpdump -w redwood-dump.pcap port 443 and host api.redwood.inference` (only if allowed by their security). That lets us inspect TLS record flow and whether a FIN came from client or server.

sam: I'll open an internal escalation with ops and include the customer's trace files once they upload. Meanwhile sending instructions to customer with a compact checklist.

jenny: Checklist to send to customer (copyable):
1) Exact curl command (copy/paste).
2) curl-trace.txt (`--trace-ascii`) attached.
3) headers.txt (`--dump-header`) attached.
4) Timestamp window (UTC) for the request.
5) Network path details (proxy hostname/port, corporate NAT).
6) If possible, tcpdump pcap.
7) Note whether non-stream endpoint succeeds (`/v1/outputs`).

sam: sending now. will update thread when we get their bundle :thumbsup:
